inputs.text: A Wisconsin jury found Harry Wait guilty of requesting ballots for Robin Vos and Cory Mason without their consent—a serious breach, whatever one thinks of his stated motive. He said he was trying to expose weaknesses in the voter-registration system, but taking matters into his own hands was not a lawful way to defend election integrity. The system should be secure enough to withstand scrutiny, and officials should answer legitimate questions plainly; still, claims about vulnerabilities don’t excuse fraud or identity theft. Wait was convicted of two misdemeanor election-fraud charges and one felony identity-theft charge, while acquitted of another identity-theft count.
